Subject: Deployment mode decision & cost sensitivity — AtlasGrid next steps

Hi Leah / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size a concise pilot and a short procurement path.

1) What we heard (high level)
- Primary goal: deliver low-latency recommendations inside AtlasGrid’s customer UI during searches (95th perc target < 180ms).
- Expected steady traffic: ~120k requests/day, concentrated 09:00–19:00 PT (bursty peaks ~2.5x).
- Typical context sizes: prompts ~120–450 tokens, average response ~180 tokens; heavy reuse of cached prefixes for 60% of requests.
- Controls & constraints: SOC 2 evidence required, SSO + SCIM, and data residency in us-west region.

2) Fit by deployment mode (short guidance)
- Hosted API: fastest path to production, works well for variable traffic and if per-token economics are acceptable. Good for 30–90 day proof-of-value.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): recommended if you need predictable latency at peak and want lower unit cost for steady traffic. Best when you can commit to a monthly/annual baseline.
- Private VPC / on-prem: required only if AtlasGrid must keep inference inside customer network for compliance. Longer setup and higher TCO but necessary for regulated data flows.

3) Rough cost sensitivity (ballpark scenarios — see attached workbook for line-item math)
- Hosted (per-token): generation rate example (avg output 180 tokens) => $0.0005–$0.0009 per generated token depending on model tier and concurrency. For 120k req/day this maps to ~$22k–$40k/month in gross hosting costs (pre-discounts).
- Dedicated (reserved): example commitment: 2 x A100-equivalent pools + autoscale buffer. Fixed commit ~ $18k–$28k/month; effective per-request unit cost can fall 30–50% vs hosted for steady workloads.
- Private VPC: one-time infra + setup + higher baseline monthly costs; operating costs comparable to Dedicated when fully utilized but heavier up-front.

Notes: numbers above are preliminary. The attached AtlasGrid_TCO_Workbook.xlsx models three scenarios (pilot, steady-state hosted, steady-state dedicated) with toggles for cache hit rate, model size, and concurrency.

4) Proposed next steps
- Internal ask from AtlasGrid: confirm expected monthly active requests and an acceptable pilot budget.
- Redwood: run an initial 2-week pilot (hosted) instrumented for latency and token counts OR run a dedicated pilot with a short reserved burst if AtlasGrid can commit to a 3-month evaluation.
- Security: we’ll share SOC 2 evidence and a Private VPC checklist (marissa will loop in engineering).

Can you confirm which pilot flavor you prefer (hosted quick pilot vs. short dedicated burst)? If hosted, we can stand up instrumentation within 48 hours after access is granted.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the TCO workbook and a suggested pilot kickoff timeline.

—Karthik

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications so we can pick a pilot: 

- Our traffic pattern on pilot will be ~15k requests/day (subset of customers), but we expect the production ramp to be ~6–8x over six months.
- Cache reuse is high for recommendations (about 65% prefix reuse), which should materially reduce token spend.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required; we also need SAML SSO + SCIM integration.

Pilot preference: hosted first for speed, but we’d like a plan for a dedicated transition if the pilot meets latency and cost gates.

Can you send the workbook and a one-page checklist for security prerequisites and a draft pilot success criteria? Procurement looped in for cost visibility.

Thanks — Leah
